name: Exodus

facts.author: Moses. The book says that Moses wrote down the words of the Lord (24:4), and the Jewish people and the early church held that he wrote the whole book.
facts.audience: The people of Israel, newly set free from Egypt and on their way to the promised land

about: Exodus means "going out". The book begins long after the death of Joseph. Jacob's family has grown into a great people, but a new Pharaoh makes them slaves. God hears their cry and calls Moses from a burning bush, telling him His name, I AM (3:14), and sending him to lead Israel out.

When Pharaoh refuses to let the people go, God sends ten plagues on Egypt. On the night of the Passover the blood of a lamb on the doorposts saves the firstborn of Israel (12:13), and God then opens the Red Sea for His people to cross. At Mount Sinai He makes a covenant with them and gives them the Ten Commandments and His laws.

The people soon break the covenant by worshipping a golden calf, but God forgives them through Moses' prayers. The book ends with the tabernacle built just as God commanded, and the glory of the Lord filling it (40:34).

themes.title: God the Redeemer
themes.text: God sets His people free from slavery by His mighty power, and the Passover lamb shows how He saves them from judgement.

themes.title: The covenant and the law
themes.text: At Sinai God makes Israel His own people and gives them His commandments, beginning with the call to have no other gods (20:2-3).

themes.title: God among His people
themes.text: The tabernacle is the place where the holy God lives among Israel and where they meet with Him.

themes.title: Sin and mercy
themes.text: Israel complains and turns to an idol, yet God shows Himself merciful and gracious and renews His covenant (34:6-7).
